title: Why we procrastinate and what to do about it, with Fuschia Sirois, PhD

sentences.en: You know the old saying, never put off until tomorrow what you can do the day after tomorrow?
sentences.zh: 你知道那句老话吗？“今天能做的事，何必拖到后天呢？”

sentences.en: Ah, yes, procrastination.
sentences.zh: 啊，是的，拖延症。

sentences.en: No one feels good about it, but most of us do it at least occasionally.
sentences.zh: 没人喜欢这种感觉，但我们大多数人至少偶尔会这样做。

sentences.en: You might have a big work project that's due, you feel stressed about it, and suddenly you realize you can't possibly get started until you clean your desk.
sentences.zh: 你可能有一个重要的工作项目要完成，你为此感到压力，突然你意识到，在清理办公桌之前，你根本无法开始工作。

sentences.en: Then you need a snack, then maybe a quick walk to clear your head.
sentences.zh: 然后你需要吃点零食，接着可能需要散个步来清醒一下头脑。

sentences.en: Oh, and don't you need to finish solving Wordle before you can tackle that job?
sentences.zh: 哦，还有，在处理那项工作之前，你不觉得得先玩完 Wordle 游戏吗？

sentences.en: Before you know it, hours have passed and you're right where you started, and more stressed than ever.
sentences.zh: 不知不觉中，几个小时过去了，你又回到了原点，而且比以往任何时候都更加焦虑。

sentences.en: Why is it so easy to fall into this trap, even when we know better?
sentences.zh: 为什么即使我们明知不对，却还是这么容易陷入这个陷阱？

sentences.en: According to some psychologists, the answer is not that people are lazy or have poor time management skills.
sentences.zh: 根据一些心理学家的说法，答案并不是因为人们懒惰或缺乏时间管理技能。

sentences.en: Instead, research suggests that procrastination is a problem driven by our emotions, and learning to manage negative emotions effectively can help us overcome it.
sentences.zh: 相反，研究表明，拖延是一个由情绪驱动的问题，学会有效地管理负面情绪可以帮助我们克服它。

sentences.en: So why do people procrastinate?
sentences.zh: 那么，人们为什么会拖延呢？

sentences.en: What tasks are they most likely to avoid?
sentences.zh: 他们最容易逃避哪些任务？

sentences.en: How does procrastination affect people's lives and their mental and physical health?
sentences.zh: 拖延如何影响人们的生活以及他们的身心健康？

sentences.en: Why is procrastination so tied up with guilt and shame, even though it's something nearly everyone does?
sentences.zh: 为什么拖延总是与内疚和羞耻感紧密相连，尽管这几乎是每个人都会做的事情？

sentences.en: And when we're faced with the temptation to put something off, how can we change our mindset and our environment to help us buckle down and do what needs to be done?
sentences.zh: 当我们面临推迟某事的诱惑时，我们该如何改变心态和环境，以帮助自己静下心来完成该做的事？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Fuchsia Sirwa, a professor of psychology at Durham University in the United Kingdom
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是英国杜伦大学心理学教授福西亚·瑟瓦博士，

sentences.en: and author of the book, Procrastination, What It Is, Why It's a Problem, and What You Can Do About It, published in July by APA Books.
sentences.zh: 她也是今年七月由美国心理学会出版社出版的《拖延：它是什么，为什么是个问题，以及你能做些什么》一书的作者。

sentences.en: She is a social, health, and personality psychologist who is broadly interested in how self-regulation,
sentences.zh: 她是一位社会、健康和人格心理学家，广泛关注自我调节，

sentences.en: how we manage our thoughts, emotions, and behaviors affect our health and well-being.
sentences.zh: 即我们如何管理自己的思想、情绪和行为，以及这些如何影响我们的健康和幸福感。

sentences.en: In addition to studying procrastination, she also researches perfectionism, self-compassion, gratitude, time, and loneliness.
sentences.zh: 除了研究拖延症，她还研究完美主义、自我同情、感恩、时间和孤独感。

sentences.en: She believes in the importance of communicating psychological science to the public to improve people's lives
sentences.zh: 她坚信向公众传播心理科学对于改善人们生活的重要性，

sentences.en: and has been interviewed about procrastination for news outlets including the Washington Post, the New York Times, and the BBC.
sentences.zh: 并曾就拖延症问题接受过《华盛顿邮报》、《纽约时报》和英国广播公司等新闻媒体的采访。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining me today, Dr. Sirwa.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天参加我们的节目，瑟瓦博士。

sentences.en: Oh, thanks for having me, Kim.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你邀请我，金。

sentences.en: I'm really thrilled to be here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, let's not put it off any longer.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们别再拖延了。

sentences.en: How do you define procrastination in your research?
sentences.zh: 在您的研究中，您是如何定义拖延的？

sentences.en: What's the difference between procrastinating and simply deferring something for another time?
sentences.zh: 拖延与仅仅将某事推迟到以后再做有什么区别？

sentences.en: Is there a difference?
sentences.zh: 这二者有区别吗？

sentences.en: There is indeed a difference.
sentences.zh: 确实有区别。

sentences.en: I want to start with a quote that a colleague and friend of mine who got me into this area of research,
sentences.zh: 我想先引用一位带我进入这个研究领域的同事兼朋友的话，

sentences.en: Tim Pitchell at Carleton University in Canada, one that he often uses to make the distinction between procrastination and delay.
sentences.zh: 他是加拿大卡尔顿大学的蒂姆·皮切尔，他经常用这句话来区分拖延和推迟。

sentences.en: And procrastination is a form of delay.
sentences.zh: 拖延是一种推迟的形式。

sentences.en: So, we can say that, you know, all procrastination is delay, but not all delay is procrastination.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们可以说，所有的拖延都是推迟，但并非所有的推迟都是拖延。

sentences.en: And really what that means is that procrastination is a very specific type of delay.
sentences.zh: 真正意味着的是，拖延是一种非常特殊的推迟类型。

sentences.en: And how, you know, researchers in the field, how we define it so that we can go out and explore, you know,
sentences.zh: 该领域的科研人员是如何定义它的，以便我们能够去探索，

sentences.en: what are the consequences and causes of procrastination, we define procrastination as an unnecessary form of delay.
sentences.zh: 探索拖延的后果和原因，我们将拖延定义为一种不必要的推迟形式。

sentences.en: It's a delay that's voluntary.
sentences.zh: 这是一种自愿的推迟。

sentences.en: So, it's not like there's an emergency.
sentences.zh: 所以，并不是因为发生了紧急情况。

sentences.en: It's not like somebody pulled you off of what you were doing, right?
sentences.zh: 也不是因为有人把你从正在做的事情中拉开了，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you've chosen to delay, and there's no really good reason to.
sentences.zh: 所以，是你自己选择了推迟，而且并没有什么真正好的理由。

sentences.en: And it's usually on a task that we said we're going to do.
sentences.zh: 而且这通常发生在我们承诺要做的任务上。

sentences.en: So, we have an intention to do that task.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，我们有完成该任务的意图。

sentences.en: We said, I'm going to do that.
sentences.zh: 我们说过，我要做那件事。

sentences.en: I'm going to clean out the garage this weekend.
sentences.zh: 这个周末我要清理车库。

sentences.en: I'm going to write that report by Friday.
sentences.zh: 周五前我要写完那份报告。

sentences.en: And that's the other thing, too.
sentences.zh: 还有一点也是如此。

sentences.en: It's usually a task that holds some importance.
sentences.zh: 这通常是一项具有一定重要性的任务。

sentences.en: And I think that lays into the final part of the definition, which is that we engage in this type of unnecessary, voluntary delay of these intended tasks,
sentences.zh: 我认为这构成了定义的最后一部分，即尽管知道这样做会对自己和他人产生负面后果，我们还是会对这些预定的任务进行这种不必要的、自愿的推迟。

sentences.en: despite knowing there will be negative consequences for ourselves and others.
sentences.zh: 尽管知道会有负面后果，我们还是会进行这种不必要的、自愿的推迟。

sentences.en: Most people procrastinate occasionally, but some people struggle with it more than others do.
sentences.zh: 大多数人偶尔会拖延，但有些人比其他人更受其困扰。

sentences.en: Do you know what percentage of people are chronic procrastinators to the point where it's really affecting their health?
sentences.zh: 你知道有多少比例的人是慢性拖延者，以至于严重影响了他们的健康吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And indeed, a lot of us can procrastinate, you know, just occasionally, which we would call sort of, you know, more of a situationally based procrastination.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们很多人偶尔都会拖延，这我们可以称之为基于情境的拖延。

sentences.en: You might procrastinate in your health, but you may not procrastinate at work, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，你可能在健康问题上拖延，但在工作上却不拖延。

sentences.en: Or you may just do it from time to time, you know, depending on the circumstances.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能只是根据具体情况偶尔为之。

sentences.en: And so, some of the estimates, the rough estimates we've gotten for that versus somebody who procrastinates on a fairly regular basis,
sentences.zh: 因此，对于那些相当频繁地拖延的人，我们得到了一些粗略的估计，

sentences.en: almost to the point where it's like part of their personality, right?
sentences.zh: 几乎到了像他们性格一部分的程度，对吧？

sentences.en: We can almost look at it like a personality trait.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎可以把它看作一种人格特质。

sentences.en: That percentage of the population in student samples, for example, college and university students,
sentences.zh: 在学生样本中，例如学院和大学的学生，

sentences.en: it's estimated about 50% of college and university students procrastinate chronically,
sentences.zh: 据估计，大约 50% 的大学生是慢性拖延者，

sentences.en: whereas about anywhere between 80 to 95% procrastinate at least once or more, but not necessarily to a large degree.
sentences.zh: 而大约 80% 到 95% 的人至少有过一次或多次拖延，但不一定达到严重程度。

sentences.en: So, it's actually quite high in college and university samples.
sentences.zh: 所以，在学院和大学样本中，这个比例确实相当高。

sentences.en: When we shift over and we look at adults, you know, who are now out in the workforce, you know,
sentences.zh: 当我们转向观察已经进入职场的成年人时，

sentences.en: they've got their degrees and they're out there, you know, just getting on with their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们已经拿到了学位，正在继续他们的生活。

sentences.en: It's still fairly high in terms of the chronic procrastination.
sentences.zh: 在慢性拖延方面，这个比例仍然相当高。

sentences.en: And again, estimates there range between 15 to 25%, which is still quite a few people who are really, you know,
sentences.zh: 同样，估计范围在 15% 到 25% 之间，这仍然有相当多的人，他们真的在

sentences.en: engaging in procrastination as a fairly regular way of dealing with tasks that they don't want to deal with.
sentences.zh: 把拖延作为处理不想面对的任务的一种相当常规的方式。

sentences.en: Well, the crux of your research is that procrastination is not, as so many of us think it is, a problem of laziness or poor time management.
sentences.zh: 您的研究核心在于，拖延并不是像我们许多人认为的那样，是一个懒惰或时间管理不善的问题。

sentences.en: Instead, it's a problem, as you say, of emotion regulation.
sentences.zh: 相反，正如您所说，这是一个情绪调节的问题。

sentences.en: So, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 那么，这意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: What does emotion regulation have to do with procrastination?
sentences.zh: 情绪调节与拖延有什么关系？

sentences.en: So, yeah, I mean, there's a lot of myths out there about why people procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 是的，关于人们为什么会拖延，外面有很多误区。

sentences.en: And, you know, sort of the common wisdom out there is that, oh, you know, teach somebody to manage their time better and they'll stop procrastinating or give them better
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为，哦，教某人更好地管理时间，他们就会停止拖延，或者给他们更好的

sentences.en: self-control or tell them they're lazy and crack the whip and get them going and that'll reduce it.
sentences.zh: 自控力，或者告诉他们很懒，鞭策他们，让他们行动起来，这样就能减少拖延。

sentences.en: And really, you know, that sort of perspective is more of looking at the symptoms of procrastination rather than the cause.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这种观点更多是在关注拖延的症状，而不是原因。

sentences.en: And this is what, as you mentioned, emotions are at the core of procrastination.
sentences.zh: 正如您提到的，情绪是拖延的核心。

sentences.en: And this comes from a lot of the research that suggests that the type of tasks that we procrastinate on are ones that we don't enjoy.
sentences.zh: 这来自于大量的研究，这些研究表明，我们拖延的任务通常是我们不喜欢的任务。

sentences.en: They're ones that we find unpleasant, aversive, and that can range the full spectrum from just simply boring
sentences.zh: 它们是我们觉得不愉快、令人反感的任务，范围从简单的无聊

sentences.en: to gut-wrenching, you know, nerve-wracking and, you know, anxiety-provoking.
sentences.zh: 到令人揪心、伤脑筋和引发焦虑的任务。

sentences.en: So, anywhere along that spectrum of tasks that makes us feel that and these negative emotions in one form or another,
sentences.zh: 所以，在这一系列任务中，任何让我们产生这种负面情绪的任务，

sentences.en: those are the tasks that we're more likely to procrastinate on.
sentences.zh: 都是我们更有可能拖延的任务。

sentences.en: And so, when we look at procrastination then in terms of emotion regulation,
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们从情绪调节的角度来看待拖延时，

sentences.en: one way to think about it is that we're not avoiding the task per se.
sentences.zh: 一种思考方式是，我们并不是在逃避任务本身。

sentences.en: What we're avoiding is the negative emotions associated with that task.
sentences.zh: 我们逃避的是与该任务相关的负面情绪。

sentences.en: And so, procrastination becomes a way to cope with that negative mood and those negative emotions,
sentences.zh: 因此，拖延成为了一种应对那种负面情绪和负面感受的方式，

sentences.en: especially if you're someone who hasn't had a lot of experience managing your negative emotions effectively,
sentences.zh: 特别是如果你是一个在有效管理负面情绪方面经验不足的人，

sentences.en: or maybe you've got a lot of other stressors going on in your life that, you know,
sentences.zh: 或者你的生活中还有很多其他压力源，

sentences.en: you've sort of your resources, your inner resources for coping with a task that might be really unpleasant or stressful or frustrating or creates a lot of worry for you.
sentences.zh: 你应对一项可能非常令人不快、压力巨大、令人沮丧或让你非常担忧的任务的内在资源已经耗尽了。

sentences.en: So, you know, in those sorts of situations, you might resort to procrastination because what procrastination does is it gives you immediate relief.
sentences.zh: 所以，在那种情况下，你可能会诉诸拖延，因为拖延能给你带来即时的解脱。

sentences.en: That's why we say it's a sort of a short-term mood repair.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们说这是一种短期情绪修复。

sentences.en: It gives you that quick fix.
sentences.zh: 它给了你那种快速的慰藉。

sentences.en: So, you take that task that's really stressing you out.
sentences.zh: 所以，你把那项让你压力巨大的任务放在一边。

sentences.en: You've got that report you've got to write.
sentences.zh: 你有一份必须写的报告。

sentences.en: You're worried about what your manager is going to think because maybe, you know, promotion rides on it or you're worried if you're going to be doing it correctly
sentences.zh: 你担心你的经理会怎么想，因为也许升职取决于它，或者你担心自己是否能正确完成，

sentences.en: or if you're going to do it as perfectly as what you want.
sentences.zh: 或者是否能达到你想要的完美程度。

sentences.en: And you take that task, you put it aside and you get busy with other things.
sentences.zh: 于是你把任务放在一边，开始忙别的事情。

sentences.en: And you've now had this immediate sense of relief.
sentences.zh: 你现在立刻感到了一种解脱。

sentences.en: You know, you've actually just repaired that negative mood and you feel better.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你实际上刚刚修复了那种负面情绪，感觉好多了。

sentences.en: And the problem with that is it's immediately reinforcing.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，这是即时强化的。

sentences.en: You get rewarded for doing that.
sentences.zh: 你因为这样做而得到了奖励。

sentences.en: And this is where some people can get caught in the trap of, you know, procrastination is almost a chronic habit or way of dealing with these unpleasant tasks.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么有些人会陷入陷阱，拖延几乎成了一种慢性习惯，或者处理这些不愉快任务的方式。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's how the emotions are involved.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这就是情绪参与其中的方式。

sentences.en: It's really about the emotions that are associated with the task and not necessarily the unpleasantness of the task.
sentences.zh: 这确实是关于与任务相关的情绪，而不一定是因为任务本身令人不快。

sentences.en: It doesn't have to be objectively an unpleasant task, but it's what our interaction with that task, you know,
sentences.zh: 它不一定客观上是一项令人不快的任务，而是我们与该任务的互动，

sentences.en: the emotions that arise from that interaction and how it makes us feel.
sentences.zh: 这种互动产生的情绪以及它让我们产生的感觉。

sentences.en: And if it's something unpleasant and we can't quite work through those feelings, procrastination becomes a way to solve that, at least in the short run.
sentences.zh: 如果这是一件令人不快的事情，而我们无法处理好这些感受，拖延就成了解决问题的一种方式，至少在短期内是这样。

sentences.en: So, what are some strategies or techniques to combat procrastination and just get things done?
sentences.zh: 那么，有哪些策略或技巧可以对抗拖延并把事情做好呢？

sentences.en: And how does thinking of it as an emotion regulation problem change how we approach the situation?
sentences.zh: 将拖延视为情绪调节问题，如何改变我们处理这种情况的方式？

sentences.en: Well, I think that's, you know, that's really key.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这非常关键。

sentences.en: If we want to address any type of problem, we've got to know what the core cause is.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想解决任何类型的问题，我们必须知道核心原因是什么。

sentences.en: And if we, you know, coming at it from this mood regulation or emotion regulation perspective,
sentences.zh: 如果我们从这种情绪调节的角度来看待它，

sentences.en: then what that suggests is that we need to find ways to manage those emotions first and foremoSt.
sentences.zh: 那么这就意味着我们需要首先找到管理这些情绪的方法。

sentences.en: And there's multiple layers of doing this.
sentences.zh: 这样做有多个层面。

sentences.en: I think, you know, especially if it's a task that's really creating a lot of stress and really a lot of frustration or anxiety or anticipated anxiety.
sentences.zh: 我认为，特别是如果这是一项确实会产生很大压力、挫败感、焦虑或预期焦虑的任务。

sentences.en: Sometimes that's not how we feel right now, but we're anticipating that as soon as we, you know, start working on those tasks, we're going to get frustrated.
sentences.zh: 有时我们现在的感觉并非如此，但我们预料到一旦开始处理这些任务，就会感到沮丧。

sentences.en: And that's enough to keep us from getting going with it.
sentences.zh: 而这足以阻止我们开始行动。

sentences.en: So, you know, finding ways to manage those negative emotions, especially if they're really intense, is key.
sentences.zh: 所以，找到管理这些负面情绪的方法，特别是如果它们非常强烈的话，是关键。

sentences.en: And some very simple ways that the research is borne out, you know, that takes sort of the edge off them is forgiveness and self-compassion.
sentences.zh: 研究证实了一些非常简单的方法，可以减轻这些情绪，那就是宽恕和自我同情。

sentences.en: And it sounds counterintuitive because, you know, you know, collectively we like to think about, you know, sort of productivity and just, you know, crack the whip and get going.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有悖常理，因为我们通常倾向于考虑生产力，鞭策自己行动起来。

sentences.en: And if somebody is not being productive and procrastinating, we think if we push them harder
sentences.zh: 如果有人没有效率并且在拖延，我们认为如果我们给他们施加更大的压力，

sentences.en: and get on their case, then they'll actually be more productive rather than saying, hey, it's okay, you know, and taking more of a compassionate approach.
sentences.zh: 严厉对待他们，他们反而会更有效率，而不是说，嘿，没关系，采取一种更具同情心的方法。

sentences.en: And actually, the research suggests that those, both those approaches can be very beneficial
sentences.zh: 实际上，研究表明这两种方法都非常有益。

sentences.en: forgiving, you know, students who forgave themselves for procrastinating on academic work were found two weeks later to actually procrastinate less.
sentences.zh: 那些原谅自己在学业上拖延的学生，两周后发现他们的拖延行为确实减少了。

sentences.en: And we know that self-compassion is, can be a very powerful tool for regulating negative emotions.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，自我同情是调节负面情绪的强大工具。

sentences.en: And that's another approach too, especially if we're really struggling and just say, you know, it's not, it's not giving yourself a free pass.
sentences.zh: 这也是另一种方法，特别是当我们真的很挣扎时，这并不是给自己找借口。

sentences.en: It's basically saying, hey, yeah, I'm not, you know, I'm struggling with this task.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是在说，嘿，是的，我在处理这项任务时很吃力。

sentences.en: I'm having difficulty, but you know what?
sentences.zh: 我有困难，但你知道吗？

sentences.en: It's okay.
sentences.zh: 没关系。

sentences.en: Um, other people have struggled with this task too.
sentences.zh: 其他人也曾在这个任务上挣扎过。

sentences.en: Um, there's nothing special about my struggle.
sentences.zh: 我的挣扎没什么特别的。

sentences.en: I just need to kind of work through that rather than, you know, getting hard on my, you know, getting hard on myself or beating myself up about this, um, and making it worse, which
sentences.zh: 我只需要克服它，而不是对自己严厉苛责，或者因为这件事而自责，这只会让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: actually can make it worse.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这会让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: The more that, you know, you get more critical about yourself about procrastinating, that can actually increase the chances that you'll continue to procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 你对自己拖延的行为越是苛刻，实际上就越有可能继续拖延下去。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You get into that endless feedback loop.
sentences.zh: 你陷入了无休止的反馈循环中。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: So how does chronic procrastination affect people's mental and physical wellbeing?
sentences.zh: 那么慢性拖延如何影响人们的身心健康呢？

sentences.en: Um, has a huge impact on it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，影响非常巨大。

sentences.en: And I think, you know, this is a thing a lot of people don't think about when they think about procrastination, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为，这是很多人在想到拖延时不会考虑的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: We think about the immediate damage it can cause.
sentences.zh: 我们想到的是它可能造成的直接损害。

sentences.en: So if you're a student and you're procrastinating your academic work, then it's likely you're not going to do as well performance wise.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一名学生，你在学业上拖延，那么你的表现很可能不会太好。

sentences.en: You're going to hand in things late or you're not going to do your best work.
sentences.zh: 你会迟交作业，或者无法发挥出最好的水平。

sentences.en: And the research bears this out, you know, people, students who chronically procrastinate tend to have poor performance in terms of their grades.
sentences.zh: 研究证实了这一点，慢性拖延的学生在成绩方面往往表现较差。

sentences.en: Um, and in the workplace as well, um, people who chronically procrastinate or procrastinate regularly, um, don't get, don't progress through their company as well.
sentences.zh: 在职场中也是如此，慢性拖延或经常拖延的人在公司里的晋升并不顺利。

sentences.en: Um, they tend to also have more, um, insecure, you know, uh, job status.
sentences.zh: 他们往往也有更不稳定的工作状态。

sentences.en: In other words, they're jumping from job to job and they never really advance much.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们频繁跳槽，却从未真正取得多大进步。

sentences.en: And they actually make less money than, than people who don't, um, chronically procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 而且他们赚的钱实际上比那些没有，嗯，长期拖延习惯的人要少。

sentences.en: And there's been some research on that.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点已经有一些研究了。

sentences.en: So we tend to think of the productivity side of it, but a lot of what I've, my research has focused on over the last couple of decades is, is exactly what you said.
sentences.zh: 所以我们往往会从生产力的角度去考虑这个问题，但我过去几十年研究的重点，很大程度上正是你所说的这一点。

sentences.en: There's these real health consequences that procrastination can be bad for your health.
sentences.zh: 拖延症确实会对健康产生负面影响，它对你的健康有害。

sentences.en: And so, um, we know it's associated with, um, you know, higher rates of depression and anxiety, definitely higher rates of stress.
sentences.zh: 我们知道它与抑郁症和焦虑症的高发病率有关，压力水平也绝对更高。

sentences.en: Um, that's one thing I found consistently, not just in with students that I've research, done research with, but also adults out in the community.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是我一直发现的一点，不仅是在我研究的学生中，在社区里的成年人中也是如此。

sentences.en: Um, and it can have very real physical health effects.
sentences.zh: 而且它可能会产生非常真实的身体健康影响。

sentences.en: Um, and this makes some sense if we think about how harmful stress is to our bodies, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我们考虑到压力对我们身体的危害有多大，这其实是有道理的，对吧？

sentences.en: Not just it's harmful for our mental health, it's also harmful for our physical health.
sentences.zh: 它不仅对我们的心理健康有害，对我们的身体健康也有害。

sentences.en: It makes, it has an impact on our immune system, makes us more vulnerable, um, you know, to,
sentences.zh: 它会影响我们的免疫系统，使我们更容易受到，嗯，你知道，

sentences.en: to catching bugs and flus and colds and all kinds of other stress-related, um, illnesses.
sentences.zh: 更容易感染病毒、流感、感冒以及各种其他与压力相关的疾病。

sentences.en: And this is something that I, I've found in my own research too, that students who chronically
sentences.zh: 这也是我在自己的研究中发现的，那些长期

sentences.en: procrastinate tend to report more of these sort of stress-related, um, you know, mild health complaints.
sentences.zh: 拖延的学生往往会报告更多这类与压力相关的轻微健康问题。

sentences.en: Uh, but they also can impact, you know, engaging in health behaviors.
sentences.zh: 但它们也会影响你参与健康行为的能力。

sentences.en: So if you're, you know, changing your diet, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在改变饮食习惯，对吧？

sentences.en: Something that can be unpleasant, right?
sentences.zh: 这可能是一件不愉快的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to give up some foods that you really enjoy, getting off the, the, you know, the couch and, and away from the screen and, and getting out and doing physical exercise if
sentences.zh: 你必须放弃一些你真正喜欢的食物，离开沙发，远离屏幕，如果你不习惯的话，

sentences.en: you're not used to it, that can be unpleasant to start too.
sentences.zh: 走出去进行体育锻炼，刚开始可能也会让人不舒服。

sentences.en: And so, you know, it's not surprising that we find that people chronically procrastinate
sentences.zh: 所以，我们发现那些长期拖延的人，

sentences.en: also tend to put off engaging in those health-promoting behaviors that would really, um, help their health overall.
sentences.zh: 往往也会推迟进行那些真正有助于他们整体健康的健康行为，这并不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Um, so if you put those two things together, higher stress, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你把这两件事结合起来，压力更大，对吧？

sentences.en: And poor health behaviors, and you tie that in with somebody who's got this pattern of, of dealing with unpleasant tasks in this very avoidant manner by, um, procrastinating over
sentences.zh: 再加上不良的健康行为，再结合某人以这种回避的方式处理不愉快任务的模式，即通过拖延，

sentences.en: time, there's going to be some cumulative damage.
sentences.zh: 久而久之，就会产生一些累积性的损害。

sentences.en: And although, you know, I've only done one study in this area, one study that I did do looking at people with, um, heart, their, their heart health.
sentences.zh: 虽然我只在这个领域做过一项研究，一项关于人们心脏健康的研究。

sentences.en: So in terms of having hypertension or cardiovascular disease, I found that those who scored higher
sentences.zh: 在患有高血压或心血管疾病方面，我发现那些在慢性拖延量表上得分较高的人，

sentences.en: on a measure of chronic procrastination, um, when you controlled for all kinds of other
sentences.zh: 在控制了所有其他可能导致心脏健康状况不佳的因素后，

sentences.en: factors that might account for poor heart health, um, you know, they were more likely, um, to, to be in the group that had poor heart health.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能属于心脏健康状况不佳的那一组。

sentences.en: I think it worked out to, um, the extent that, um, you, they had a one point increase on this measure.
sentences.zh: 我想结果是，他们在这个量表上的得分每增加一分，

sentences.en: So it was a self-report measure that we use.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我们使用的自我报告量表。

sentences.en: We ask people about, you know, how often they procrastinate or if they're putting things off to tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们询问人们拖延的频率，或者他们是否把事情拖到明天。

sentences.en: So for every one point, um, increase on that measure, their chances of having poor heart health increased by 63%.
sentences.zh: 所以该量表每增加一分，他们心脏健康状况不佳的几率就会增加63%。

sentences.en: Um, and that's after accounting for a lot of other factors.
sentences.zh: 而且这是在考虑了许多其他因素之后得出的结论。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, but, you know, it makes sense though too, because if you're stressed all the time and you're not looking after your health, these healthy behaviors and stress and health
sentences.zh: 但这也说得通，因为如果你一直处于压力之下，又不注意健康，这些健康行为和压力是通往健康的两条关键途径。

sentences.en: behaviors are two key pathways to, to good health.
sentences.zh: 而当你不去践行这些行为时，我们知道它们就是心脏健康状况不佳的风险因素。

sentences.en: And when you don't engage in them, we know that they are risk factors for poor heart health.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为这在几十年里属于极端情况。

sentences.en: Um, so, you know, I mean, that's, I think that's kind of, you know, the extreme case over, over several decades.
sentences.zh: 所以既有短期的健康影响，也有一些更严重的长期健康影响。

sentences.en: So there's short-term health impacts, but there's also some more serious long-term health impacts as well.
sentences.zh: 刚才你提到了沙发和屏幕，能够远离这些东西。

sentences.en: So a moment ago, you mentioned, um, the couch and the screen, being able to get away from those things.
sentences.zh: 我想知道社交媒体和电子设备的普及是否对拖延症有影响？

sentences.en: I'm wondering whether you know, does the ubiquity of social media and electronic devices have an impact on procrastination?
sentences.zh: 还是说拖延者总是能找到借口来推迟事情？

sentences.en: Or have procrastinators always been able to find excuses to put things off?
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: That's a great question.
sentences.zh: 有一些拖延症研究人员专门研究这一点，专门研究社交媒体和数字干扰。

sentences.en: Um, you know, there's, there, there are a lot of, there's some procrastination researchers that look just at that, just looked at the, you know, sort of social media and digital
sentences.zh: 他们的整个研究项目都在这个领域。

sentences.en: distractions.
sentences.zh: 确实存在联系。

sentences.en: Um, and, and that's their whole research program is in that area.
sentences.zh: 容易拖延的人确实倾向于使用更多的社交媒体，倾向于沉迷于数字干扰。

sentences.en: And there is indeed a connection.
sentences.zh: 而且这其中可能也存在一些代际影响，对吧？

sentences.en: So people who are prone to procrastination do tend to use more social media, tend to be, you know, engaged with their digital distractions.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，我们肯定还有其他方式来拖延。

sentences.en: Um, and you know, there might be some generational influences there too, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你看看像“睡前拖延”这样的现象，这是一种特殊的拖延形式，你会说，嘿，我明天早上有个重要的会议。

sentences.en: But that being said, you know, there's other things that we can do to engage in procrastination for sure.
sentences.zh: 我打算11点睡觉。

sentences.en: And if you look at something like bedtime procrastination, which is a particular form of procrastination where you say, Hey, I've got an important meeting tomorrow morning.
sentences.zh: 结果现在已经是凌晨1点了，你还在刷社交媒体，

sentences.en: I'm going to go to bed at 11 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能坐着看小说，或者在织毛衣。

sentences.en: And here we are 1 a.m.
sentences.zh: 所以那些研究人们如何进行睡前拖延的研究人员发现，这不仅仅是数字化的干扰。

sentences.en: in the morning and you're still on your social media, um, you know, or, or you may be sitting up reading that novel or you may be knitting that sweater.
sentences.zh: 他们会做各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: So the researchers that have looked at what people do to procrastinate on their bedtimes, it's not just digitally oriented distractions.
sentences.zh: 有些人甚至会烘焙。

sentences.en: They engage in a whole bunch of things.
sentences.zh: 这真的很奇怪。

sentences.en: Some of them bake even.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，无论你喜欢什么，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, it's, it's really bizarre.
sentences.zh: 这都是为了让你从那些你本该处理的任务所带来的情绪中分心，而那个任务就是睡觉，对吧？

sentences.en: So I think it's, you know, whatever your fancy is, right?
sentences.zh: 也许是因为你还没有处理好当天发生的事情。

sentences.en: You know, it's something to distract you from the emotions that you're not dealing with about the tasks that you should be doing, which is going to bed, right?
sentences.zh: 但这又回到了情绪调节的问题上。

sentences.en: And maybe it's because you, you know, you haven't processed what went on in that day.
sentences.zh: 我认为数字媒体确实让某些代际的人更容易拖延。

sentences.en: Um, but you know, that again, there's, it's an emotion regulation issue.
sentences.zh: 而我认为其他代际的人可能会同样找到其他类型的干扰和活动来参与。

sentences.en: And I think, yeah, the digital media makes it easier for certain generations.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有趣的是，我交谈过的很多人，当我提到我在做拖延症研究时，很多人都会告诉我他们的拖延故事。

sentences.en: And I think that other generations might find equally find other, um, you know, types of distractions and activities to engage in.
sentences.zh: 你会听到很多不同的事情。

sentences.en: And in fact, anecdotally, a lot of the people I've talked to, when I say I do procrastination research, I get a lot of people telling me about the procrastination story.
sentences.zh: 我记得我采访过一位记者，他说，是的，我记得，

sentences.en: So you hear a lot of different things.
sentences.zh: 当我在大学读书时，

sentences.en: And, you know, I remember there was one journalist I spoke to and, um, he said, yeah, I remember,
sentences.zh: 我讨厌打扫卫生，但我每当有大型论文考试临近时，天哪，我的房子打扫得可干净了。

sentences.en: you know, when I was a student in university and, um,
sentences.zh: 所以，他没有去学习，而是在忙着把房子打扫得一尘不染。

sentences.en: you know, I hate cleaning, I hate cleaning house, but whenever I had a big paper exam coming, boy, was I, my house ever clean.
sentences.zh: 你经常会看到这种情况。

sentences.en: And so, you know, and so instead of doing studying, he was running around getting, you know, the house perfectly clean.
sentences.zh: 拖延者并不是坐在那里偷懒。

sentences.en: And you see this a lot.
sentences.zh: 他们在做其他事情。

sentences.en: It's not like procrastinators sitting around lazy.
sentences.zh: 只是没有做当下那件迫在眉睫、重要且如果不完成就会产生负面后果的事情。

sentences.en: They're doing other things.
sentences.zh: 在准备这次谈话时，我当然去谷歌搜索了一下谁是著名的拖延者。

sentences.en: It's just not that thing that they should be doing right now that's looming and important and will have negative consequences if they don't get it done.
sentences.zh: 正如你可能看到的那样，有很多名单，其中包括达赖喇嘛、弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特、赫尔曼·梅尔维尔、列奥纳多·达·芬奇等名人。

sentences.en: In prepping for this conversation, I, of course, had to go to Dr. Google and find out who are famous procrastinators.
sentences.zh: 撇开这些名单在历史上是否准确不谈，它们提出了一个问题：一个人既是慢性拖延者，又极其高产，这可能吗？

sentences.en: And there are lists, as you've probably seen them, and they include luminaries like the
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: Dalai Lama, Frank Lloyd Wright, Herman Melville, Leonardo da Vinci.
sentences.zh: 我想，我会回到这一点：他们是真的在拖延，还是在进行某种形式的延迟？

sentences.en: Putting aside whether these lists are historically accurate, they raise the question, is it possible to be a chronic procrastinator, but also extremely productive?
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是“明智的延迟”，当某人推迟某事时，表面上看，我们可能会说，嘿，他们在拖延。

sentences.en: That is a really good question.
sentences.zh: 或者我们甚至会审视自己的行为。

sentences.en: And I think, yeah, I mean, I would go back to, well, were they really procrastinating or were they engaging in some other form of delay?
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为这是一种延迟，而我们没有做我们知道应该做的事情，我们可能会说，我在拖延。

sentences.en: You know, so we talk about sagacious delay where on the surface, when somebody puts something off, we might look at them and say, hey, they're procrastinating.
sentences.zh: 但如果你深入观察，可能你还没有开始那份报告，是因为你在等待一些关键信息，而这些信息对于你开始工作至关重要。

sentences.en: Or we might even look at our own behavior.
sentences.zh: 如果你在没有这些信息的情况下就开始了，实际上是在浪费大量时间。

sentences.en: And just because it's a delay and we're not doing what we know we should be doing, we might say, well, I'm procrastinating.
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: But if you sort of look below the surface, it may be that maybe you haven't started that report because you're waiting to hear back with some key information that's essential
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们确实必须在延迟和拖延之间做出区分。

sentences.en: for you to get going on this.
sentences.zh: 可能确实存在一些非常重大的延迟者，但他们可能是明智的延迟者，是有目的地在做这件事。

sentences.en: And if you started without that information, you actually would be wasting a lot of time.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 我认为那些真正与拖延症作斗争的人，他们的处境很糟糕。

sentences.en: And so I think we really do have to make that distinction between delay and procrastination.
sentences.zh: 他们有职业问题、健康问题。

sentences.en: There might be some really, you know, monumental delayers out there, but they could be sagacious delayers, wise delayers who are doing it with purpose.
sentences.zh: 他们没有实现梦想或达到目标。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，与其从生产力的角度来定义它，我认为这助长了我们许多关于我们应该或不应该做什么、应该或不应该做多少的社会规范，

sentences.en: And I think the people that I've spoken to who really struggle with procrastination, they are in a bad way.
sentences.zh: 我更愿意围绕人们是否达到了目标，或者你是否有很多事情开始了却从未完成来定义它。

sentences.en: They have career issues, health issues.
sentences.zh: 你是否有很多未实现的愿望，只是因为恐惧、失败，或者担心做得不够好，或者担心在处理任务时无法应对可能面临的挑战，而一直没有去完成？

sentences.en: They're not fulfilling their dreams or not reaching their goals.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这些所谓的著名拖延者可能根本不是拖延者，我觉得有趣的是，我看到的名单上女性并不多。

sentences.en: So, you know, rather than frame it in terms of productivity, which I think feeds into a lot of our social norms about who we, you know, what we shouldn't and shouldn't be doing
sentences.zh: 出现了几个名字。

sentences.en: and how much we shouldn't and shouldn't be doing.
sentences.zh: 例如玛格丽特·阿特伍德、J.K.罗琳，她们也是高产的，但如果这些名单有任何真实性的话，我们是否应该认为女性比男性拖延得少？

sentences.en: I'd rather frame it around people's, you know, whether you're reaching your goals or not, or do you have all these things you started and never finished?

sentences.en: So, and, you know, there is some research, there's some procrastination researchers down in Peru, and we do these conferences every couple of years, and just sort of, you know,

sentences.en: regularly, because they see their managers and their bosses procrastinating.

sentences.en: And the tolerance there for procrastination is, is quite low.

sentences.en: You also study perfectionism, which is a topic that we recently talked about on another episode of this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 你还研究完美主义，这也是我们最近在播客的另一期节目中讨论过的话题。

sentences.en: I just want to ask if perfectionism and procrastination are linked, and are perfectionists more or less likely to procrastinate?
sentences.zh: 我想问一下完美主义和拖延症之间是否有联系？完美主义者更容易还是更不容易拖延？

sentences.en: No, great question.
sentences.zh: 不，这是个很好的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think, you know, first thing I have to say is that perfectionism isn't sort of a single entity.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想说，首先我必须指出，完美主义并不是一个单一的概念。

sentences.en: We have these sort of different subcategories or dimensions of perfectionism.
sentences.zh: 我们有不同类别的完美主义，或者说完美主义的不同维度。

sentences.en: So there's this thing called perfectionistic concerns, which is sort of a self-critical type of perfectionism, where the person has really high, you know, standards for themselves
sentences.zh: 有一种叫作“完美主义顾虑”，这是一种自我批判型的完美主义，这类人对自己有极高的标准，

sentences.en: and is really driven to try and please other people.
sentences.zh: 而且非常有动力去取悦他人。

sentences.en: And, you know, their self-worth is contingent upon whether they live up to some sort of idealized standard that they think society or their friends or their family expect of them.
sentences.zh: 他们的自我价值感取决于他们是否达到了社会、朋友或家人所期望的某种理想标准。

sentences.en: And then you've got this other flavor of perfectionism, which is this perfectionistic strivings,
sentences.zh: 还有另一种类型的完美主义，叫作“完美主义追求”，

sentences.en: which is more someone who's driven by their own internal standards, but these standards are still quite high.
sentences.zh: 这类人更多是受自身内部标准的驱动，但这些标准依然相当高。

sentences.en: And so because of that, they might sort of not be able to savor their successes when they actually reach those standards.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，当他们真正达到这些标准时，反而可能无法享受成功的喜悦。

sentences.en: And so we actually conducted some research a couple years ago where we did this thing called a meta-analysis, which is just basically a review of all the research that's ever been

sentences.en: done looking at the associations between perfectionism, both perfectionism dimensions there, and procrastination.
sentences.zh: 旨在观察完美主义（包括上述两个维度）与拖延症之间的关联。

sentences.en: And we had, you know, 40-some-odd studies that included 10,000 people.
sentences.zh: 我们分析了四十多项研究，涵盖了一万名受试者。

sentences.en: And when we looked at the links between chronic procrastination and perfectionism, we indeed found
sentences.zh: 当我们观察慢性拖延与完美主义之间的联系时，我们确实发现，

sentences.en: that individuals who were more prone to chronic procrastination also scored higher on this measure of the self-critical perfectionism.
sentences.zh: 那些更容易出现慢性拖延的人，在自我批判型完美主义的量表上也得分更高。

sentences.en: However, there wasn't a link with the other form of perfectionism.

sentences.en: So I sort of lay that out there because it's slightly different there.

sentences.en: I can say yes and no because no to one type, but yes to another.
sentences.zh: 我可以说是，也可以说不是，因为对于一种类型来说不是，但对于另一种来说是。

sentences.en: Um, and I think it makes sense though too, because if you're really driven and your whole sense

sentences.zh: 所以这也是为什么，至少在我的研究中，我默认的方法是观察那些有慢性拖延倾向的人，因为在某种意义上，我们把“拖延”这个变量固定住了，

sentences.zh: 然后我们观察他们会有什么样的想法？

sentences.en: we're looking at what are the sort of thoughts that they have?
sentences.zh: 他们会经历什么样的后果，对吧？

sentences.zh: 我的一些学生曾尝试让人们在某个时间点填写问卷，
